mechanisms.description: An order whose only command revokes, vacates, restores or relinquishes is performed when it issues and is spent on issue (coordinator ruling P1); an order whose only command amends another merges into the parent on issue and its text lives or ends with the parent (ruling P2).

Relinquishment under the Act of July 5, 1884: the President places reservation lands found useless for military purposes under the Secretary of the Interior for disposal. The order ends the military reservation over the lands it names.

A later executive order that revokes, vacates, rescinds or supersedes the member by number or date, or relinquishes all of the member's lands, ends it. Version 1 uses 25 such orders whose texts are held (23 are members of this family; EO 7320 and EO 9293 are not).

Philippine independence, through instruments whose words reach reservations: sec. 10(a) of the 1934 Act ('including all military and other reservations', except naval reservations and fueling stations), Proclamation 2695 of July 4, 1946, Article I of the Treaty of General Relations (in force October 22, 1946; excepting bases retained by agreement), and the 1947 Military Bases Agreement, which fixed the retained bases in Annexes A and B. Members at retained bases need the instrument that relinquished the base.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: interval from the order date to 1947-03-26 for places not retained; none for retained bases

mechanisms.description: End of the Canal Zone and of U.S. rights there: the Panama Canal Treaty of 1977 entered into force on October 1, 1979; defense sites stayed in U.S. use under the Agreement in Implementation of Article IV until the Treaty terminated at noon on December 31, 1999.

sources.citation: Philippine Independence Act (Tydings-McDuffie Act), Act of Mar. 24, 1934, ch. 84, secs. 5 and 10, 48 Stat. 456, 459, 463
sources.title: Philippine Independence Act
sources.pin: including all military and other reservations
sources.establishes: Section 10(a) directed the President, on the July 4 after ten years of the Commonwealth, to withdraw and surrender all U.S. possession, jurisdiction, control or sovereignty over the Philippine Islands, 'including all military and other reservations of the Government of the United States in the Philippines (except such naval reservations and fueling stations as are reserved under section 5)'; section 10(b) left naval reservations and fueling stations 'in its present status' pending negotiation.

sources.citation: Proclamation No. 2695, Independence of the Philippines, July 4, 1946, 60 Stat. 1352, 1353
sources.title: Proclamation 2695
sources.pin: hereby withdraws and surrenders
sources.establishes: On July 4, 1946, acting under the 1934 Act and 'subject to the reservations provided for in the applicable statutes', the President withdrew and surrendered all U.S. rights of possession, supervision, jurisdiction, control or sovereignty over the territory and people of the Philippines.

sources.citation: Treaty of General Relations between the United States and the Republic of the Philippines, signed July 4, 1946, art. I, 61 Stat. 1174 (ratifications exchanged and in force Oct. 22, 1946)
sources.title: Treaty of General Relations (Treaty of Manila) 1946
sources.pin: except the use of such bases, necessary appurtenances to such bases
sources.establishes: Article I (read on the web, not held) withdraws and surrenders all U.S. rights of possession, supervision, jurisdiction, control or sovereignty over the Philippine Islands, except the use of such bases as the United States may by agreement with the Republic deem necessary to retain; the treaty entered into force on October 22, 1946.

sources.citation: Joint Resolution of June 29, 1944, ch. 322, sec. 2, 58 Stat. 626 (22 U.S.C. 1392)
sources.title: Philippine bases joint resolution
sources.pin: withhold or to acquire and to retain such bases
sources.establishes: Authorized the President, after negotiation, to withhold or acquire and retain bases in the Philippines in addition to those provided for by the 1934 Act; it explains why some Army reservations were not surrendered on July 4, 1946 (read on the web through 22 U.S.C. 1392, not held).

sources.citation: Panama Canal Act of 1979, Pub. L. 96-70, secs. 3(b)(1), 1504 and 3304, 93 Stat. 452, 455, 488, 500
sources.title: Panama Canal Act of 1979
sources.pin: shall be deemed to refer to the areas and
sources.establishes: From the date the Panama Canal Treaty of 1977 entered into force (sec. 3304), 'Canal Zone' in U.S. law is deemed to refer to the areas and installations in the Republic of Panama made available to the United States under the Treaty (sec. 3(b)(1)); the Zone as U.S.-controlled territory in which the President set apart reservations ceased on that date.

sources.citation: Panama Canal Treaty, signed Sept. 7, 1977, arts. II, IV, XI, 33 U.S.T. 39, T.I.A.S. No. 10030, 1280 U.N.T.S. 3 (No. 21086); in force Oct. 1, 1979
sources.title: Panama Canal Treaty of 1977
sources.pin: shall reassume plenary jurisdiction over the former Canal Zone
sources.establishes: The Treaty came into force on October 1, 1979; on entry into force it terminated and superseded the Isthmian Canal Convention of 1903 (art. I(1)(a)) and Panama reassumed plenary jurisdiction over the former Canal Zone on entry into force; U.S. military use of defense sites thereafter rested on the separate Agreement in Implementation of Article IV; the Treaty terminated at noon, Panama time, December 31, 1999 (read on the web in the UNTS copy, not held).

sources.citation: Act of July 5, 1884, ch. 214, sec. 1, 23 Stat. 103
sources.title: Abandoned Military Reservations Act
sources.pin: to be placed under the control of the Secretary of the Interior for disposition
sources.establishes: When the President finds the lands of a military reservation, or any portion, useless for military purposes, he shall cause them to be placed under the control of the Secretary of the Interior for disposition under the Act (read on the web, not held); an order made under it relinquishes the military reservation over the lands it names.

sources.citation: Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976, Pub. L. 94-579, secs. 701(c) and 704(a), 90 Stat. 2743, 2786, 2792
sources.title: FLPMA
sources.pin: in effect as of the date of approval of this Act shall remain in full
sources.establishes: Section 704(a) repealed, from October 21, 1976, the President's implied withdrawal authority and the withdrawal sections of the Pickett Act of June 25, 1910 (36 Stat. 847); section 701(c) kept all withdrawals and reservations then in effect in full force until modified under FLPMA or other law. This is a continuity point, never an end.

sources.title: Engle Act
sources.pin: on and after February 28, 1958 the provisions hereof shall apply
sources.establishes: Requires an Act of Congress for defense withdrawals of more than 5,000 acres made on and after February 28, 1958 (read on the web through 43 U.S.C. 155, not held); it is prospective and neither ends nor confirms an earlier executive-order reservation.

sources.citation: Hawaii Admission Act, Pub. L. 86-3, sec. 5(c) and 5(e), 73 Stat. 4, 5-6 (1959)
sources.title: Hawaii Admission Act
sources.pin: shall remain the property of the United States subject only to the limitations, if any, imposed
sources.establishes: Lands set aside for federal use by Act, proclamation or executive order on the date of admission remained U.S. property (sec. 5(c)); each agency was to report within five years, and land the President found no longer needed was to be conveyed to the State (sec. 5(e)) (read on the web, not held). It is a lead for each Hawaii reservation, not an end or a continuation of any one order.

sources.citation: Agreement between the United States and the Republic of the Philippines concerning Military Bases, signed Mar. 14, 1947, arts. I, XVII, XXIX and Annexes A and B, 43 U.N.T.S. No. 673; in force Mar. 26, 1947 (Statutes at Large citation not verified)
sources.title: Military Bases Agreement 1947
sources.pin: the right to retain the use of the bases in the Philippines listed in Annex A
sources.establishes: Read on the web in the UNTS copy, not held. The Republic of the Philippines, 'in the exercise of its title and sovereignty', grants the United States the right to retain the use of the bases listed in Annex A (art. I(1)) and to use the Annex B bases when military necessity requires; the agreement came into force on March 26, 1947 for 99 years (art. XXIX). Annex A lists Clark Field Air Base and Fort Stotsenberg (Pampanga), Mariveles Military Reservation (Bataan), Camp John Hay Leave and Recreation Center (Baguio), the Army Communications System 'with the deletion of all stations in the Port of Manila Area', U.S. Armed Forces Cemetery No. 2 (San Francisco del Monte, Rizal), Angeles General Depot (Pampanga), Leyte-Samar Naval Base, Subic Bay Northwest Shore Naval Base with 'the existing Naval reservation at Olongapo and the existing Baguio Naval Reservation', Tawi Tawi Naval Anchorage, Canacao-Sangley Point Navy Base (Cavite), Bagobantay Transmitter Area and Manila-area radio sites, and four Loran stations in Palawan and Zambales; Annex B lists Mactan Island, Florida Blanca, the Aircraft Service Warning Net, Camp Wallace (La Union), Puerto Princesa (Palawan), Tawi Tawi Naval Base and Aparri. Exchange of Notes V reserves the adjustment of U.S. rights and titles to real property for later settlement.

lead.basis: Words that reach the reservation: section 10(a) of the Philippine Independence Act directs the surrender of 'all right of possession, supervision, jurisdiction, control, or sovereignty' over the Islands, 'including all military and other reservations of the Government of the United States in the Philippines (except such naval reservations and fueling stations as are reserved under section 5)'; Proclamation 2695 of July 4, 1946, 'subject to the reservations provided for in the applicable statutes', states that the United States 'hereby withdraws and surrenders all rights of possession, supervision, jurisdiction, control, or sovereignty now existing and exercised' over the territory; Article I of the Treaty of General Relations (in force October 22, 1946) withdraws and surrenders all such rights 'except the use of such bases ... as the United States of America, by agreement with the Republic of the Philippines, may deem necessary to retain'; and the agreement so made, the Military Bases Agreement in force March 26, 1947, retains only 'the use of the bases in the Philippines listed in Annex A' (and Annex B on necessity), which do not include this member's place. Member test: the reservation lies in the Philippine Islands and its place is not among the Annex A or B bases. The surrender reached Army reservations on July 4, 1946; naval reservations, left 'in its present status' by section 10(b), and any base withheld under the joint resolution of June 29, 1944, were surrendered no later than the agreement's entry into force.

date_rule.basis: July 4, 1946 for Army reservations surrendered by Proclamation 2695; no later than March 26, 1947, when the Military Bases Agreement fixed the bases retained under Article I of the Treaty of General Relations; earlier if a later order revoked or restored the lands

gaps: The Treaty of General Relations (61 Stat. 1174) and the Military Bases Agreement (43 U.N.T.S. No. 673) are read on the web only; acquire them.

Section 5 of the 1934 Act kept lands designated for 'Military and other reservations' out of the 1935 grant to the Commonwealth, and Note V of the 1947 agreement reserved 'adjustment of U.S. rights and titles to real property' for later settlement. The surrender reaches the possession, control and jurisdiction that the reservation commands; any U.S. title that outlasted it is a property question disclosed here, not a continuation of the reservation.
The joint resolution of June 29, 1944 (58 Stat. 626) is read on the web only; which bases, if any, the President withheld under it before July 4, 1946 is not established in the sources held.

For Manila members: a proclamation of July 3, 1946, printed just before Proclamation 2695 (its closing part, on the held 60 Stat. 1352 page, describes Manila properties and directs negotiation for title to any not vested in the United States; its number and opening page are not verified), dealt with certain Manila properties for U.S. use; any such use rests on that new instrument, not on the member.

lead.basis: The President set these reservations apart within the Canal Zone, or on adjacent lands whose use the 1903 Isthmian Canal Convention granted. The Panama Canal Treaty of 1977 entered into force on October 1, 1979, terminated and superseded the 1903 Convention (art. I(1)(a)), and returned plenary jurisdiction over the former Zone to Panama (art. XI); but U.S. military forces kept using defense sites under the Agreement in Implementation of Article IV, a new instrument that excepts that property from the transfer (coordinator ruling P5). The Treaty, and with it every U.S. right to use areas in the former Zone, terminated at noon, Panama time, December 31, 1999 (art. II: 'This Treaty shall terminate at noon, Panama time, December 31, 1999'). The Panama Canal Act of 1979 (held) treats 'Canal Zone' thereafter as the areas in the Republic of Panama made available under the Treaty (sec. 3(b)(1)) but contains no words ending these reservations earlier.

date_rule.basis: termination of the Panama Canal Treaty of 1977 at noon on 1999-12-31 (art. II); earlier if a later order superseded or rescinded the member

gaps: The Panama Canal Treaty (1280 U.N.T.S. No. 21086) and the Agreement in Implementation of Article IV are not held; the Treaty was read on the web only. Acquire both.
A member whose land passed to Panama on October 1, 1979 (outside the defense sites) ended then; identifying those needs the Article IV agreement's annexes.

lead.basis: Many of these reservations (for example Fort Shafter, Fort DeRussy, Fort Ruger, Schofield-area and Pearl Harbor tracts) may still be federal land. Section 5(c) of the Hawaii Admission Act kept lands set aside by executive order as U.S. property, and section 5(e) required conveyance to the State of lands found no longer needed; neither fixes the status of any one order.

gaps: Current federal real property or Army/Navy installation records for each tract, and section 5(e) conveyance records, would decide yes or no; acquire the Hawaii Admission Act text.

lead.basis: A reservation for military, naval or departmental use stands until revoked, relinquished, transferred or disposed of. FLPMA sec. 701(c) kept every withdrawal and reservation in effect on October 21, 1976 in full force until modified, and sec. 704(a) repealed only the authority to make new ones; the Engle Act of 1958 is prospective. None of these ends or confirms a member. Many National Guard ranges were later revoked by executive orders or Public Land Orders; some reservations (for example Fort Sill, Fort Bliss ranges) may still be military land.

gaps: A yes needs a current predicate: a statute naming the reservation, or current BLM (MLRS/LR2000) withdrawal records or DoD real property records showing the order's lands still reserved under it. A no needs the revoking order, Public Land Order, statute or surplus-property deed naming the order or its lands.
